I have from eternity from the Father, before I became man; but when I became man, I received it temporally according to the humanity, and kept it hidden until my resurrection and ascension, when it had to be made manifest and declared. Just as Paul also says in Romans 1: 'He was declared to be the Son of God with power' [Rom. 1:4]. John 17 calls it glorification." Similar testimonies are found in the writings of Dr Luther, especially in the book, "That these words are still firm," and in the great confession concerning the Lord's Supper. To those writings, or to the well-founded declarations of the majesty of Christ at the right hand of God, and of his testament, we refer, for the sake of brevity, in this article, as also in the article on the Lord's Supper, as has been said.

units.la: Quare perniciosum errorem iudicamus, Christo secundum suam humanitatem tantam maiestatem detrahere, qua Christianis ingens consolatio detrahitur: quam in illa promissione de præsentia & inhabitatione sui capitis, regis & sacerdotis habent: qui ipsis promisit, quòd non tantū sua nuda Deitas ipsis adesse velit: quæ erga nos peccatores tanquam consumens ignis est in aridas stipulas: sed ille ipse homo, qui cum ipsis locutus est, qui omnes afflictiones in sua assum pta natura expertus est, qui etiam nobiscum tanquam hominibus & fratribus & suis cō dolecscere potest, velit nobiscum esse in omnibus nostris necessitatib. etiam secundū eā natura qua noster frater est, & nos caro de carne ipsius sumus.
units.tr: Therefore we judge it a pernicious error to detract from Christ according to his humanity so great a majesty, by which great comfort is taken away from Christians: which they have in that promise of the presence and indwelling of their head, king and priest, who promised them that he would be present to them not merely with his bare Deity, which towards us sinners is like a consuming fire among dry stubble, but that the very man who spoke with them, who has experienced all afflictions in his assumed nature, who can also sympathise with us as with men and brothers and his own, would be with us in all our necessities, even according to that nature by which he is our brother and we are flesh of his flesh.

units.la: Itaque reiicimus & damnamus vnanimiter ore & corde, omnes errores à prædicta doctrina discrepantes, tanquam pugnantes cum scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis, cum veris symbolis, & cum nostra quoque confessione Augustana.
units.tr: Therefore we unanimously reject and condemn, with mouth and heart, all errors differing from the aforesaid doctrine, as contrary to the prophetic and apostolic writings, to the true creeds, and also to our Augsburg Confession.

units.la: 1 Veluti si quis in hoc argumento crederet, aut à quoquam edoctus esset, Humanam naturam propter hanc hypostaticam vnionem permixtam esse Diuinitati, aut in eam mutandam fore.
units.tr: 1. As if someone in this matter believed, or were taught by anyone, that the human nature, on account of this hypostatic union, is mixed with the Deity, or is to be changed into it.

units.la: 2 Item Naturam humanam in Christo præsentem vbique esse sui ipsius viribus essentialibus & proprietatibus nature suę, eodem prorsus modo quo Diuinitas, id est, tan quam essentia infinita.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, that the human nature present in Christ is everywhere by its own essential powers and properties of its nature, in exactly the same way as the Deity, that is, as an infinite essence.

units.la: 3 Item, Humanam naturam in Christo cuasisse similem naturæ Diuinæ substantia, essentia, vel suis proprietatibus essentialibus.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, that the human nature in Christ has become like the substance, essence, or essential properties of the divine nature.

units.la: 4 Item humanitatem Christi esse in omnibus locis cœli & terræ localiter extensam. (quod ne Diuinæ quidem naturæ tribuendum est) sed Christum omnipotentia sua Diuina posse corpore suo præsentem esse vbicunque voluerit, maxime vero vbi expressis verbis promisit se futurū, veluti in sacra Cœna. Quum enim corpus suum ad dexteram Maiestatis & potentiæ Dei collocauerit, potest vtique id efficere virtute & sapientia sua: non mutata aut diuisa vera sua humana natura.
units.tr: 4. Likewise, that the humanity of Christ is extended locally in all places of heaven and earth (which is not to be attributed even to the divine nature), but that Christ, by his divine omnipotence, can be present with his body wherever he wishes, most of all where he promised expressly that he would be, as in the holy Supper. For since he has placed his body at the right hand of the majesty and power of God, he is certainly able to do this by his virtue and wisdom, without his true human nature being changed or divided.

units.la: 5 Item, Quod sola humanitas passa sit pro nobis nosq. redemerit: Nec vllam cum illa in ipsa passione filius Dei communicationem vera habuerit.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, that the humanity alone suffered for us and redeemed us, and that the Son of God had no true communion with it in that very passion.

units.la: 6 Item, Christum secundum suam Diuinitatem duntaxat interius nobis præsentem esse in prædicatione verbi & in legitimo sacrorum sacramentorum vsu, hancque præsentiam nullo modo pertinere ad naturam humanam.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, that Christ is present to us inwardly according to his Deity alone, in the preaching of the Word and in the lawful use of the sacred sacraments, and that this presence does not pertain at all to the human nature.

units.la: 7 Item, Humanam naturam Christi nullam reuera effectualem communionem habere cum virtute, potentia, sapientia, Maiestate, & gloria Dei, sed nomine & titulo tenus duntaxat cum illa communicare.
units.tr: 7. Likewise, that the human nature of Christ has no real effectual communion with the power, might, wisdom, majesty and glory of God, but communicates with it only in name and title.

units.la: Hos inquam errores omnesque eiusmodi alios, supradictę doctrinæ aduersantes, repudiamus tanquam puro Dei verbo scriptisque Prophetarum & Apostolorum ac Christianæ nostræ fidei confessionisque cōtrarios. Et omnes Christianos hortamur quandoquidē CHRISTVS mysterium in Scriptura sacra nominatur ne in huiusmodi mysteriis (etiamsi hæretici de illis plurimum se torqueat & fatigent) inquirendis rationem suam scru pulosius intendant, sed simpliciter cum dilectis Apostolis credant, oculos rationis obturent, intellectúmque suum captiuum ad obedientiam Christi deducant: sese consolentur & assiduè gaudeant quod caro sanguisque nostra ita sint in Christo ad dexterā maiestatis & omnipotentiæ Dei euecta. Id si fecerint, certam firmámque consolationem in omnis generis afflictionibus comperient, erúntque aduersus omnes perniciosos errores munitissimi.
units.tr: These errors, I say, and all others of this kind opposed to the aforesaid doctrine, we repudiate as contrary to the pure Word of God, to the writings of the Prophets and Apostles, and to our Christian faith and confession. And we exhort all Christians, since Christ is named a mystery in holy Scripture, not to strain their reason too scrupulously in inquiring into such mysteries (even if heretics wear themselves out and weary themselves much over them), but simply to believe with the beloved Apostles, to shut the eyes of reason, and to lead their captive understanding into obedience to Christ; let them console themselves and continually rejoice that our flesh and blood are thus exalted in Christ to the right hand of the majesty and omnipotence of God. If they do so, they will find a certain and firm consolation in every kind of affliction, and they will be most well fortified against all pernicious errors.

units.la: Versio hæc multos habet Germanismos, quod in multis verba ipsa authorum reddere oportuerit, ne quid in sensu mutatum videretur. Hoc excusabit benignus lector.
units.tr: This translation has many Germanisms, because in many places it was necessary to render the authors' own words, lest anything seem changed in sense. The kind reader will excuse this.

units.la: CONSILIVM EORVNDEM THEOLOGORVM DE RATIONE auctoritatis illi scripto in Germanicis Ecclesiis, extra Synodum, conciliandæ.
units.tr: THE ADVICE OF THE SAME THEOLOGIANS ON HOW TO RECONCILE THE AUTHORITY OF THAT WRITING IN THE GERMAN CHURCHES, OUTSIDE THE SYNOD.

units.la: ILLVSTRISIME Princeps, optata imprimis Celsitudini vestræ Dei gratia per Christum, & simul nostrûm omnium humillimo, promptissimo atque supplici obsequio precibúsq. præmissis. Notum Celsitudini vestræ cũ omni reuerentia facimus, quod cũ proxima dominica, Exaudi, hoc est die xix. huius mensis Maij Bergæ, prope Magdeburgum simul conuenissemus, nihil nobis prius fuit quàm vt statim in eo conuentu diligentissimè Torgensis illa Concordię formula, cum omnibus ad ditamentis & animaduersionibus hinc inde adscriptis à nobis perlegeretur & expenderetur: studioséque cogitaremus qua ratione mense Martio proximè elapso, ex illis omnes magis necessariæ vtilêsque sententiæ in Torgense illud scriptum suo queque loco insertæ ac veluti incorporatæ aliæque etiam nonnullæ additæ fuerint. Adeo vt tandem
units.tr: Most illustrious Prince, may your Highness first be wished, by God's grace through Christ, every good thing, and we all offer our most humble, most ready and suppliant service and prayers. We make known to your Highness, with all reverence, that when we had met together at Berga, near Magdeburg, on the Sunday next before Ascension, Exaudi, that is on the 19th day of this month of May, nothing was more pressing for us than to read through and weigh, at that meeting and with the greatest care, the Torgau formula of concord, together with all the additions and remarks made on both sides. We also considered carefully how, in the month of March just past, all the more necessary and useful opinions from those additions had been inserted, each in its proper place, into that Torgau writing and, as it were, incorporated into it, and how some others had been added. So that at last

units.la: C.iiij.
units.tr: C.iiij.

units.la: ex iis omnibus vndique collectis (nullibi tamen vero ac Christiano sensu mutato) vnū voluměn cōfecerimus. Cuius Exemplar à nobis subscriptum C. V. reuerenter ac demisse nunc offerimus: certissima fiducia spéq. ducti fore vt id piis omnibus Doctoribus satisfaciat, qui incorruptæ doctrinæ Verbi Dei (qualem Deus omnipotens per beatæ memoriæ Doctorem Lutherum in lucem reuocare dignatus est) firmiter adhærent, nec sese hodiernis doctrinis opinionibúsque abripi clam patiuntur.
units.tr: from all these things gathered together from every side (yet nowhere changing the true and Christian sense) we have made one volume. A copy of it, subscribed by us, we now offer to your Highness with reverence and humility, being led by a most certain confidence and hope that it will satisfy all the pious teachers who firmly cling to the uncorrupted doctrine of the Word of God (such as Almighty God deigned to bring back to light through the teacher of blessed memory, Luther), and who do not allow themselves to be carried off secretly by present-day doctrines and opinions.

units.la: Quum autem propter quorundam adiectas animaduersiones factum sit vt non pe-ræq. omnes prolixæ illi Declarationi Torgæ conceptæ acquieuerint: perlegimus etiā atque diligenter expendimus illius summa-riam Epitomen: Conuenitque inter nos tandem vt illa epitome maiori illi operi siue for-mulæ Torgensi præponeretur: quod non sine maxima fiet vtilitate. Hinc enim statim Christianus lector animaduertere & perspi-cere poterit qua de re in singulis articulis cōtrouertatur: quidque ex auctoritate verbi Dei in iis credi, vel non credi debeat, & sic deinceps vtilius faciliúsque prolixam illam Declarationem percipiet.
units.tr: Since, however, on account of the additional remarks of certain men it has come about that not nearly all of them have agreed to that long Declaration drawn up at Torgau, we have also read through and carefully weighed its summary Epitome. And it has at last been agreed among us that this Epitome should be placed before that larger work, or the Torgau formula, which will be of the greatest use. For from it the Christian reader can at once see and perceive on what matter there is controversy in each article, and what ought or ought not to be believed in them on the authority of the Word of God; and so he will afterwards grasp that long Declaration more usefully and easily.

units.la: Quia porro Celf. V. hoc quoque nobis benignè iniunxit vt inuicem colloqui & conferre,ac etiam statuere vellemus quonam pacto ista Theologis reliquorum ordinum Augustanæ confessionis, cùm generalis Synodus conuocata fuerit, proponenda, vlteriúsque in hoc toto negotio progrediendum censeamus. Denique vt vbi de singulis ad hoc tam salubre opus promouendum necessariis, aut vtilibus consultauerimus, id totum C. V. significemus, dissimulare certè istud apud C. V. nō debemus, Nihil fore nobis optatius nec amabilius, quàm si ea esset omnium Ministrorū Augustanæ confessionis apud omnes ordines qui eam profitentur consensio: vt ex iis omnibus Christiana synodus sine periculo grauiorum dissidiorum ac controuersiarum, cogi posset. In qua de rebus Ecclesiæ magis necessariis ac salutaribus simul consilia inirentur.
units.tr: Moreover, since your Highness has also kindly enjoined on us that we should confer and consult with one another, and also decide how these matters are to be put before the theologians of the other orders of the Augsburg Confession when a general Synod has been convened, and how we should proceed further in this whole business, and finally, when we have taken counsel on any of the things necessary or useful for promoting this so salutary work, that we should report all of it to your Highness: we must certainly not conceal from your Highness that nothing would be more desirable or more pleasing to us than that there should be agreement of all the ministers of the Augsburg Confession among all the orders which profess it, so that from all of them a Christian synod could be convened without danger of more serious dissensions and controversies. In it counsels might be taken at the same time on the more necessary and salutary matters of the Church.

units.la: Verùm, heu, nimium nobis compertum est (vel ex additamentis ad Torgense illud scriptum adiectis) esse adhuc in plerisque locis plerosque Ecclesiarum Ministros qui circa Doctrinam prorsus morosos ac pertinaces sese præbeant: sed & Principes nonnullos in illis regionibus eiusmodi opinionibus & præiudiciis imbutos esse, maximè suspicamur. Si ergo tanta frequentia ac multitudo Theologorum conueniret. Et ex iis quidam (etsi forte pauciores) alij in alios insurgeret, suósve Magistratus animarent, aut ab illis ipsi in suis opinionibus obfirmarentur, neque vllus inter nos consensus obtineri posset, sed ita alij ab aliis re infecta discedere cogerentur: satis animaduertere potest V. C. quantùm inde lętitiæ non solum Sacramentarij sed & Papistæ cōcepturi essent: quámque graues in Ecclesiis nostris apud pios hinc offensiones oriri possent. neque enim quicquid ibi gestū fuerit silentio obtegetur aut occultum esse poterit. Itaque nostra quidem hæc est sententia tutius omnino fore & extra omne periculum si prius Christianæ Concordiæ subscriptio ab aliis Augustanæ confessionis ordinib. scripto aut per literas exigatur. Cuius nostri consilij executio hoc pacto posset institui.
units.tr: But, alas, we have found out too well (even from the additions made to that Torgau writing) that there are still in many places many ministers of the Churches who show themselves most stubborn and obstinate about doctrine; and we especially suspect that some princes in those regions are imbued with such opinions and prejudices. If therefore so great a crowd and multitude of theologians should assemble, and some of them (perhaps fewer) should rise against others and encourage their magistrates, or should themselves be confirmed in their opinions by them, and no agreement could be obtained among us, but the others were forced to depart from one another with the matter unsettled, your Charity can readily see how much joy would then be conceived not only by the Sacramentarians but also by the Papists, and how grave offences might arise from this among the pious in our Churches. For whatever was done there would not be covered by silence, nor could it remain hidden. Therefore our opinion is that it will certainly be safer and free of all danger if first the subscription to the Christian Concord is demanded in writing or by letter from the other orders of the Augsburg Confession. The execution of this our counsel could be carried out in the following way.

units.la: Primum vt subscriptio hæc ante omnes exigatur à Theologis qui penes eos status residet, quos certò constat ex ipsorum adiectamentis purioris esse doctrinæ, quorumque haud dubiè subscriptio mox subsequetur. Quales sunt imprimis ambarum Celsitudinum Vestrarum: itémque, nunc Dei gratia, Illustrissimi Electoris Ludovici Palatini, TheoTheologi: per quos ipsius Celsitudo Consi- storia sua atque Ecclesias in toto Palatinatu nuper Christiane restaurauit. Deinceps vero ab iis qui sunt in inferiore Saxonia, & Mechelburgensi, Luneburgensi, atque Brunsvvicensi ditione, Item in Grubenha- gio, simulque in maritima Saxoniæ parte, ac Ciuitatibus illi adiacentibus (vnica Brema nunc quidem, excepta.) Tum demum ab iis qui sunt in Franconia Germaniæ superio ris atque in Sueuia. Item in Marchionatu Georgij Friderici ad Anspach. Item in ditio- ne Comitis Palatini Philippi Ludouici, ac Palatini Comitis Ioannis, Ducis Vvirtem- bergi: Marchionis item Badensis: Tandem vero etiam à Theologis Ciuitatum liberarum superioris Germaniæ quales sunt Ratif bona, Augusta vindelicorum, Vlma, Dona- vvertum, Francofurtum, Argentina & pleraque aliæ multæ numero: De quarum (excepta Noriberga) Theologis, eorúmq. subscriptionibus dubitari non potest.
units.tr: First, let this subscription be demanded before all others from those theologians who reside in those states, whom it is certain from their own additions are of purer doctrine, and whose subscription will undoubtedly follow at once. Such are especially those of both your Highnesses, and also, now by God's grace, the theologians of the most illustrious Elector Ludwig of the Palatinate, through whom his Highness has recently restored Christianly his consistories and churches in the whole Palatinate. Then from those who are in Lower Saxony, and in the territories of Mecklenburg, Lüneburg and Brunswick, likewise in Grubenhagen, and at the same time in the maritime part of Saxony and the cities adjacent to it (only Bremen, for the present, excepted). Then at last from those who are in Franconia of Upper Germany and in Swabia; likewise in the Margraviate of George Frederick at Ansbach; likewise in the territory of Count Palatine Philip Louis, and of Count Palatine John, Duke of Württemberg; also of the Margrave of Baden. Finally, also from the theologians of the free cities of Upper Germany, such as Regensburg, Augsburg (of the Vindelici), Ulm, Donauwörth, Frankfurt, Strasbourg, and many others besides. Concerning the theologians of these cities, and their subscriptions (Nuremberg excepted), there can be no doubt.

units.la: Cum vero eiusmodi subscriptio à supra nominatis Illustrissimis Electoribus Principibúsque aliis atque liberis Ciuitatibus impetrata fuerit: posset deinde & à reliquis Imperij Ordinibus hisce rationibus exigi: si hoc quidem tempore deliberandi spatium liberum illis relinquatur quo de hoc Chri- ftiano instituto amplexando & ipsi ferio cogitent. Vbi enim illis de horu trium Illu- ftriffimorum Electorum, aliorumque Ordi- num vnanimi consensu per hanc subscri- ptionem constabit: eorumque motiuae cau- sae, quibus hactenus visi sunt retineri atque impediri, refutatae fuerint: fieri diuina me- diante gratia poterit vt & ab illis facilius eadem subscriptio impetretur.
units.tr: When such a subscription has been obtained from the above-named most illustrious Electors and other Princes, and from the free cities, it could then also be demanded from the remaining orders of the Empire on these grounds: provided that at this time a free space for deliberation is left to them, in which they may seriously consider for themselves embracing this Christian arrangement. For when it is clear, through this subscription, that these three most illustrious Electors and the other orders are in unanimous agreement, and when the motives for which they have hitherto seemed to be held back and hindered have been refuted, then, by the mediating grace of God, it may come about that the same subscription may be obtained from them more easily.

units.la: Caeterum ne diuersitas vlla in eiusmodi subscriptionibus accidere possit sub qua falsi, inquieti atque pertinaces Doctores latitare valeant: Non erit haec admonitio in eo scripto quod ad hanc subscriptionem obtinendam emittetur, praetermittenda. Vt omnes Theologi sedulo caveant ne singuli pro arbitrio in subscribendo longas periodos, quae specialem aliquam explanationem contineant, vsurpare audeat: sed nudum no-men duntaxat cum cognomine, ac loci cui seruient (siue Ecclesiae, siue scholae) designatione adscribant.
units.tr: Moreover, lest any diversity in such subscriptions can occur, under cover of which false, restless and obstinate teachers might lie hidden, this admonition will not be omitted in the writing which is sent out to obtain this subscription: that all theologians should carefully take care lest anyone presume, in subscribing at his own discretion, to add long sentences which contain some special explanation; but that they should append only the bare name with the surname, and the designation of the place which they serve (whether church or school).

units.la: Et quandoquidem aduersarii nostri Papistae tam intra quam extra Germanicae nationis Imperium Ecclesias nostras accusant, quasi vix duo in illis Concionatores reperiantur qui in omnibus Confessionis Augustanae stanæ capitibus, idem sentiant: Hæc esset nostra in eo sententia, vt in subscriptionibus obtinendis hic ordo seruetur. Vt primi quidem subscribant Doctores Theologiæ qui in Academiis ad consistoria accedunt, quò certius de illis constet quales sint, nec scilicet per ipsos falsi Doctores, in scholis, aut impuri Concionatores in templis introduci, recipiue aliquando possint.
units.tr: And since our adversaries the Papists accuse our Churches, both inside and outside the Empire of the German nation, as though scarcely two preachers could be found in them who think alike on all the chapters of the Augsburg Confession, our opinion in this matter would be that the following order be observed in obtaining the subscriptions. That first the teachers of theology who attend the consistories in the Academies should subscribe, so that it may be more certainly known what kind of men they are, and so that false teachers cannot be introduced by them into the schools, nor impure preachers into the churches, at any time.

units.la: Deinde in singulis Ciuitatibus Parochus cum suis Capellanis seu vicariis: (vbi hi desunt, superintendens cum duobus parochis ruri habitantibus) non solum proprio suo nomine sed etiam omnium aliorum parochorum, Capellanorum & scholarcharum qui ad eandem pertinent diœcesim, (modò prius ab ipsis approbationem & potestatem subscribendi obtinuerint) subscribat in hunc fere modum.
units.tr: Then in each city the parish priest with his chaplains or vicars (where these are lacking, the superintendent with two parish priests living in the country) should subscribe in roughly this manner, not only in his own name but also in the name of all the other parish priests, chaplains and schoolmasters who belong to the same diocese (provided they have first obtained from them approval and the power to subscribe):

units.la: Ego Ioannes N. parochus & superintendens apud N. & cum eo N. & N. parochum apud N. & N.N. parochi itidem N.N. illi adiuncti subscribimus tam pro nobis ipsis, quam pro N. parocho, capellano & scholarcha, qui sunt omnes numero N.N.
units.tr: I, John N., pastor and superintendent at N., together with N., pastor at N., and N.N., likewise pastor, who are joined with him, subscribe both for ourselves and for N., the pastor, chaplain and schoolmaster, that is, for all of them, N.N. in number.

units.la: Totidem fere verba nec plura possent post generales illas (Theologorum cuiusq. principatus, ac ordinis) subscriptiones ascribi, quæ non multas paginas in hoc toto opere occuparent. Et multos bonos viros forte iu uare possent,& à tam graui hæsitatione libe rare, in quam falsis Papistarum persuasionibus induci potuerunt: Quasi nullus sit omnino inter vllos Euangelicos concionato- res doctrinæ consensus.Et hoc modo multa oborta scandala tolli facile possent, quibus alioqui spiritus Dei in multorum piorum cordibus fuit magna tristitia affectus.
units.tr: Nearly this many words, and no more, could be added after the general subscriptions of the theologians of each principality and order. These would not occupy many pages in this whole work. They might help many good men and free them from the grave doubt into which the false persuasions of the Papists have led them, as if there were no agreement at all in doctrine among any evangelical preachers. In this way many scandals that have arisen could easily be removed, scandals by which, in any case, the Spirit of God has been greatly saddened in the hearts of many pious people.

units.la: In Ciuitatibus autem liberis cum non multi ibi sint Ecclesiarum ministri, Ne alij ab aliis effugij prætextum , suæ opinionis tuendæ caussa, ex eo captent, quod singuli pro seipsis non subscribant: Necesse foret omnes simul ad subscriptionem conuocari quod à Consulibus & reliquis Magistratib. facile præstari poterit.
units.tr: In free cities, however, where there are not many ministers of the churches, so that others may not seize on a pretext for escaping from one another in defence of their opinion, because individuals do not subscribe for themselves, it would be necessary to call everyone together to subscribe at once. The consuls and the other magistrates can easily secure this.

units.la: Ne porro reliqui Principes Ordinéque Imperij (qui ad hoc vsque tempus nondum suam de eiusmodi subscriptione sententiam clarè expositerunt) causari, conquerive iu- stè possint,eiusmodi subscriptionem à nobis pluralitate potius votorum illis obtrudi quàm vllo veritatis testimonio: Et omnibus potius legitimam libertatem relinquedam, qualem in Ecclesia esse & æquum & soli- tum est. Hanc inquam ob causam existermamus omnino consultius esse vt siquidem illi intra aliquod tempus clarius suam sententiam non explicabunt, sed pertinaciter in semel concepta opinione perstiterint, Ne simpliciter ab illis subscriptio mordicúsque exigatur sed scripto prius ipsorum motiuæ rationes firmissimis argumentis confutentur addatúrque necessaria admonitio firmis fundamentis subnixa, cur non potuerimus nec possimus adhuc vlla alia scripta Philippi in hoc corpus inserere quàm Augustanam Confessionem eiúsque Apologiam. Quamuis alioqui eius expressa fiat alibi mētio: Et liberum singulis tum Ecclesiis tum scholis relinquatur non minus ipsius reliquis scriptis (ad præscriptum tamen huius Declarationis siue formulæ)vti,quàm cæterorum omnium scriptorum tam nouorum quàm veterum. Qua admonitione ad ipsos missa,& subscriptione huius formulæ demū amicè expetita: si tamen adhuc semel concepte opinioni pertinaciter adhęserint, nec sese melius erudiri patiantur: erimus sanè erga ipsos debito officio functi: Et facilè tū Illustrissimi Electores, cæteríque Ordines, tum ipsorum Theologi excusationem legitimam apud omnes consequētur. Illi verò siue Principes siue Ordines qui subscribere renuerint, nullam iustæ querimoniæ occa-sionem prætexere poterunt, cùm ipsorum rationes non solum silentio non fuerint prætermisse sed etiam contrariis rationibus ex verbo Dei confutatæ.Ex quibus omnib. V.C.iam satis animaduertere & existimare potest, nos nunc quidem in hoc conuentu nullo modo statuere potuisse quomodo hæc propositio in generali synodo si quæ cogenda fuerit, Theologis Augustanæ confessionis foret proponenda. Nã cùm illa non solû ex principiis huius laudabilis ac verè Christiani operis, repetenda fit; sed & tota pendeat ex Principum ac statuum Augustanæ confessionis mente & voluntate, de qua nõdum constare ante institutam & impetratam subscriptionem potest. Eapropter cum certò coniici adhuc nequeat quis fit huius subscriptionis futurus euentus, existimamus non posse adhuc eam propositionem hoc tempore concipi, sed esse omnino eius rationes eo vsque differendas dum subscriptio fuerit impetrata. Tum enim (si quidem eo modo quem instituimus subsequetur) clarius constabit quid precipuè in eo generali conuentu proponendum foret. Neque tum valde sollicitos esse Illustrissimos Principes Electores, aliósque Ordines oportebit de contencontentionibus periculosísque illis discor- diis quæ plerunque ex eiusmodi Synodis subsequi solere, tum Ecclesiasticæ historiæ tum quotidiana experientia testantur.
units.tr: Moreover, so that the remaining princes and estates of the Empire, who up to now have not clearly set out their opinion on this kind of subscription, cannot justly complain or protest that such a subscription is being forced upon them by us through a majority of votes rather than by any testimony of truth, and that everyone should rather be left the lawful liberty that is right and customary in the Church, we think it altogether more advisable for this reason. If they do not explain their opinion more clearly within some time, but persist obstinately in the opinion once formed, then subscription should not be demanded from them simply and at all costs. Instead, their motives should first be refuted in writing by the strongest arguments, and a necessary admonition, resting on firm foundations, should be added, explaining why we have not been able, and still cannot, to insert any other writings of Philip into this corpus besides the Augsburg Confession and its Apology, although elsewhere express mention is made of him. And each church and school should be left free to use his other writings no less (yet in accordance with the prescription of this Declaration or formula) than all other writings, new and old. Once this admonition has been sent to them, and subscription to this formula has finally been sought in a friendly way, if they still cling obstinately to the opinion once conceived and will not allow themselves to be better instructed, we shall certainly have discharged our proper duty towards them. Then the most illustrious electors and the other estates, and their theologians, will easily obtain a lawful excuse in the eyes of all. Those princes or estates who refuse to subscribe will not be able to pretend any just occasion for complaint, since their reasons have not been passed over in silence but have also been refuted by contrary reasons from the Word of God. From all this Your Graces can now already perceive and judge that we in this assembly could not in any way determine how this proposal should be put before the theologians of the Augsburg Confession in a general synod, if one is to be convened. For that proposal must be drawn not only from the principles of this praiseworthy and truly Christian work, but also depends entirely on the mind and will of the princes and estates of the Augsburg Confession, which cannot yet be known before the subscription has been set in motion and obtained. Therefore, since it cannot yet be conjectured with certainty what the outcome of this subscription will be, we think that this proposal cannot yet be framed at this time, and that its grounds must be deferred altogether until the subscription has been obtained. For then (if it follows the course we have laid out) it will be clearer what chiefly ought to be proposed at that general assembly. Nor will the most illustrious electors and the other estates then need to be very anxious about those dangerous contentions and discords which, as both church history and daily experience testify, usually follow such synods.

units.la: Quod verò ad totius huius negotij exe- cutionem & cætera quæ inde pendent, atti- net, Celsitudines Vestræ satis pro sua pru- dentia per se intelligent, quibus rationibus per Dei gratiam vnio inter vos sanciri pote rit, atque vnanimi consensu prouideri, vt se rió ac diligenter in hoc omnes incumbant ne posthac cuilibet pro arbitrio concessum sit in Ecclesiis aut scholis noua certamina excitare, sed ea moderatio ordóque seruetur vbique, vt nulli iusta occasio conquerendi data videatur quasi os Spiritui sancto obstruere velitis, dum rixas ac friuolas contentiones inhibere quantum in vobis est nitimini. Hæc porro omnia, vt & pleraq. alia, in præfatione, quæ Illustrissimorum Electorum aliorúmque Principum nomine huic de controuersis capitibus formulæ & eius epitome præficienda erit, contineri ac inseri necesse est.
units.tr: As for the execution of this whole matter and what depends on it, Your Highnesses will understand well enough by your own prudence by what means, through the grace of God, unity among you can be established, and by unanimous consent provide that everyone applies himself earnestly and diligently to this, so that from now on no one is allowed at his own discretion to stir up new quarrels in the churches or schools. Instead, moderation and order shall be kept everywhere, so that no one may seem to have a just occasion for complaint, as if you wished to stop the mouth of the Holy Spirit, while you strive as far as you can to restrain strife and frivolous contentions. Moreover, all these things, and many others, must necessarily be contained and inserted in the preface which is to be placed, in the name of the most illustrious electors and other princes, before this formula on the controverted articles and its epitome.

units.la: Quum autem harum regionum Ecclesiæ & scholæ per quosdam publicè editos libel- los (veluti eo cui titulus est Grundfest.i.fun damentum: & Nouo Catechismo, aliisque eiusmodi de persona Christi tractantibus) in errorem misere sint inductae & pleraeque etiam ex illis in maximam ac periculosissi-mam dubitationem adductae, indeque sacra mentariis via in has regiones patefacta: quiique libri illi adhuc in manibus versentur multorum qui forte nondum agnoscunt le tale venenum in illis contineri: Operaepretium imo perquam necessarium iudicamus Ecclesias Dei communi aliquo Theologorum, huius praecipue regionis, scripto admonerí quid in istis libellis, manifeste aduersetur simplici fidei ac purae Doctrinae quam in his regionibus ante haec grauia schismata magno consensu Christiani Doctores ex Dei verbo sunt professi.
units.tr: Since the churches and schools of these regions have been led into error, and most of them thrown into the greatest and most dangerous doubt, by certain publicly issued little books (such as the one entitled Grundfest, i.e. Fundamentum, and the New Catechism, and others of this kind treating of the person of Christ), and since the way has thereby been opened in these regions for the sacramentarians, and since those books are still in the hands of many who perhaps do not yet recognise that such poison is contained in them, we judge it worthwhile, indeed most necessary, to admonish the churches of God by a common writing of some theologians, especially of this region, as to what in those little books plainly contradicts the simple faith and pure doctrine which Christian teachers, from the Word of God, professed with great agreement in these regions before these grave schisms.

units.la: Sic enim sperandum est fore ut non solum qui nos subsequentur ab omni errore praemoniti caveant, sed & plerique errantes in viam reuocentur: qui eiusmodi scriptis irretiti, neque seipsos neque alios inde extricare vel liberare possunt. Id vero omne breui, sincera, simplici firmisque fundamentis nitente admonitione, ex illis ipsis impuris scriptis articulatim excerpta, confici quam facillime atque expediri poterit.
units.tr: For thus it is to be hoped that not only those who follow us will be forewarned and guarded against every error, but also that many who are erring will be called back to the right way, those who are ensnared by such writings and can neither extricate nor free themselves or others from them. All this can be most easily put together and despatched in a brief, sincere, simple admonition resting on firm foundations, excerpted article by article from those very impure writings.

units.la: Quae supersunt capita maxime vero ad Typographiam spectantia per quam fit ut multi infrugiferi libri,& ad Christianam v-nitatem in Ecclesia retinendam minimè v-tiles in publicum spargantur, Et Ecclesiæ Dei multis minus necessariis, quibúsque fa-cilè caruerint,scriptis grauentur: Vtilia ve-rò multa ac præcipuè Doctoris Lutheri scri-pta ex hominum manibus excutiantur, vn-de denique exordium huius tam funestæ dif-sensionis in hisce regionib. nuper manauit. Quod præterea ad huius vnionis executio-nem pertinet,quomodo scilicet illa sit con-stituenda, & cum constituta fuerit quo pa-cto per Dei gratiam firma & constans reti-neri poterit:adeò vt nemo de iniusta vi sibi illata merito conqueri possit, & nihilo mi-nus ad obseruationem iusti alicuius ordinis omnes inducantur: Hæc, inquam, omnia nos ad præscriptam formam, quæ mense Martio proximè elapso,(cum Torgensis for-mula aut Corpus Doctrinæ emendaretur) constituta fuit,remittimus.
units.tr: The remaining heads, which relate especially to printing, through which it comes about that many unfruitful books, and books least useful for keeping Christian unity in the Church, are scattered abroad, and the Church of God is burdened with many less necessary writings, which could easily be dispensed with, while many useful writings, and especially those of Doctor Luther, are taken out of people's hands, whence at last the beginning of this so deadly dissension has recently flowed forth in these regions. Further, as regards the execution of this union, namely how it is to be established, and once established, by what means it can be kept firm and constant through the grace of God, so that no one can justly complain of unjust force being used against him, and yet all may be brought to observe some just order: all these matters, I say, we refer to the form prescribed, which was drawn up last March, when the Torgau formula or Corpus Doctrinae was being amended.

units.la: Non potuimus autem ista C. V. pro ossi-cij nostri debita executione celare. Roga-mus itaque Omnipotentem Deum ac Pa-trem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, vt virtute sancti sui spiritus dignetur totum hoc opus Christianum, (non solùm salutare & necessarium) sic ad optatum, & hactenus multorum piorum suspiriis expetitum finem perducere, quemadmodum illud feliciter in ipsius nomine cœptum, & per ipsius gratiam (Vestræ Celsitudinis nimirum opera) tam longè fuit iam perductum: nec illud vspiam quasi fixum & impeditum hærere aut retardari patiatur: sed faxit vt semel tandem aduersariis nostris pontificiis hoc scripto os ob struatur & eorum blasphemiis occurratur. Sacramentariorum etiam & aliarum sectarum errores dissipentur & misera afflictáque Ecclesia rursus ex animo exhilaretur. Cùm hoc opus vltimum fortasse vale Domini no stri Iesu Christi hoc extremo seculo futurũ sit. Quod superest Deus Optim. Max. hanc Celsitudin. Vestræ operam sine mercede es- se non patietur, sed tum temporariis tum æ- ternis benedictionibus ample cumulabit. Ec clesia verò Dei, nósq. omnes humili nostro seruitio & precibus apud Deum promerebi- mur. Cuius paterne potentissimeque tutelæ & protectioni Celsitudinem Vestram, Nos verò V. C. gratiæ ac beneuolentiæ humilli- mè commendamus.
units.tr: We could not, however, conceal these things from Your Graces, in the proper discharge of our office. We therefore ask Almighty God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ that, by the power of his Holy Spirit, he may deign to bring this whole Christian work (which is not only salutary and necessary) to the desired end, longed for until now with sighs by many pious people, just as it has been begun happily in his name and, by his grace (namely through the work of Your Highness), has already been carried so far. May he not allow it to stick or be delayed anywhere as if fixed and hindered, but grant that at last the mouths of our Papist adversaries be stopped by this writing and their blasphemies be met. May the errors of the sacramentarians and of other sects also be scattered, and the wretched and afflicted Church be cheered again from the heart. For this last work will perhaps be the farewell of our Lord Jesus Christ to this last age. As for the rest, may God, most good and greatest, not allow this effort of Your Highness to go unrewarded, but richly heap upon you both temporal and eternal blessings. We, for our part, shall earn the Church of God and all of us by our humble service and prayers before God. To the paternal and most powerful protection and guardianship of God we most humbly commend Your Highness, and ourselves to the favour and goodwill of Your Graces.

units.la: Actum Bergæ prope Magdeburgum 28. Maij Anno, &c. 1577.
units.tr: Done at Berga near Magdeburg, 28 May, in the year, etc. 1577.

units.la: C. V.
units.tr: To Your Highnesses (C. V.)

units.la: Addictissimi atque obsequentissimi servi, &c.
units.tr: Most devoted and most obedient servants, etc.

units.la: TILEMANI HESHVSII AD D. MARTINVM Chemnizium Epistola.
units.tr: TILEMANN HESHUSIUS'S LETTER TO DR. MARTIN CHEMNITZ.

units.la: ALVTEM à Filio Dei, perpetuo Ecclesiæ custode, Re. D.P. superintendens, Amice & frater in Domino dilecte. Multis modis ostēdit Filius Dei IesusChristus,se præsentem esse Ecclesiæ suę & eius fidelem agere curam: Documentum vero valde illustre est, detectio fraudum Caluinistarum, confusio persecutorum, preclarum testimonium veritati datum & mutatio dextrę excelsę in Electore Augusto. Hęc opera regnantis Christi cum aspicio, continere non possum, quin prorumpam in lętam gratiarum actionem, cum precatione vt perficiat opus preclarum, quod incœpit dextra sua. Perquam gratum mihi est, quod historiam conuentus Torgensis tam accuratè ad me perscripseris, insignis beneficij loco id pono, & vicissim mea offero officia, siqua à me proficisci possunt. Facile autem colligo moleste te ferre, quod tardius respō-demus: causę verò multę sunt, quia tempestiuè cognouimus Electorem Saxonię hu c missurum esse. Formulam concordiæ, respo- sum nostrum ad petitionem Ducis Brun- suicensis Iulij dístulimus. Vbi vero Electoris formulā accepi, statim eam descripsi curaui & legi, tradidi etiam pastoribus legendum, & D. Vvigando.
units.tr: GREETING from the Son of God, the perpetual guardian of the Church, to the Reverend Dr. P., superintendent, friend and brother beloved in the Lord. The Son of God, Jesus Christ, has shown in many ways that he is present with his Church and faithfully takes care of it. Among the clearest proofs are the exposure of the frauds of the Calvinists, the confusion of the persecutors, the noble witness given to the truth, and the change of heart in the Elector Augustus, brought about by the right hand of the exalted Christ. When I see these works of the reigning Christ, I cannot help breaking out into a joyful thanksgiving, and praying that he who has begun the noble work with his right hand will bring it to completion. I am very glad that you have written to me so carefully about the history of the Torgau convention, and I count it a remarkable kindness. In return I offer you my services, wherever I can be of use. I easily gather that you are annoyed that we have answered slowly. There are many reasons, chiefly that we learned early that the Elector of Saxony would send the Formula of Concord here. We had put off our reply to the petition of the Duke of Brunswick, Julius. But as soon as I received the Elector's Formula, I had it copied out, read it, and also handed it to the ministers to read, and to Dr. Wigand.

units.la: Nos toto pectore gratias agimus Deo, quod tam egregiū & illustre testimonium datur veritati, pro qua hactenus pugnauimus solum. Hoc tantum quæsiuimus & etiam nunc querimus, vt veritas Euangelij in corrupta sonet in Ecclesia: profligatis fanatis cis sententiis, contumeliosis in Filium Dei, & syncera Lutheri doctrina, Thesaurus mundi postremi, ad posteritatem sine fermento sectarum transferatur.
units.tr: We give heartfelt thanks to God that so noble and illustrious a testimony is borne to the truth, for which we alone have fought until now. We have sought only this, and still seek it: that the truth of the Gospel may sound forth uncorrupted in the Church, that the fanatical opinions, the insults against the Son of God, be cast out, and that the pure doctrine of Luther, the last treasure of the world, be handed down to posterity without the leaven of sects.

units.la: Quod ergo ad capita controuersiarum attinet, quæ in formula concordiæ explicantur in Thesi & Antithesi consentimus. Nec Deo nos regente suo spiritu ab hac sententia nos vnquam seiungemus. Quod si Theologi Vvitebergenses ita perpetuo docuissent, nunquam ab eis discessione fecissemus, neq. syllabā contrā eos scripsissemus. Quia vero sententiam rogamur de formula conscripta, & Inclytus Elector petit, vt sine metu liberè dicamus, si quid desideremus, candidè & modestè monemus de quibusdam, dam, non vt turbemus praeclarum opus, neque vt istouas lites moueamus, sed vt omnia quæ in hoc praeclaro libro, ac velu ti Symbolo Ecclesiæ, pias mentes offendere possunt, remoueantur, & in posterum ansæ contentionum, quantum fieri potest, præscindantur. Existimamus Ecclesiæ necessitatem postulare, vt in hac formula autores & patroni corruptelarum, Illyricus, Philippus, Pfeffingerus, Osiander, Maior, Caluinus, Petrus Martyr, EpistolaPhilippi ad Palatinum nominentur, ac Ecclefię & posteritati saltem indicentur, vt Iuuentus in librorum lectione errores cum formula concordię pugnantes cauere possit.
units.tr: As far as the chief points of controversy are concerned, which are explained in the Formula of Concord in thesis and antithesis, we agree. With God ruling us by his Spirit, we will never depart from this opinion. If the Wittenberg theologians had always taught in this way, we would never have dissented from them, nor written a single syllable against them. But since we are asked for our judgement on the drawn-up Formula, and the illustrious Elector asks that we speak freely and without fear if we desire anything, we advise frankly and modestly about certain matters. We do not do this to disturb the excellent work, nor to stir up new quarrels, but so that everything in this splendid book, which is like a creed of the Church and may offend pious minds, may be removed, and so that in future the occasions of dispute may be cut off as far as possible. We think the needs of the Church require that in this Formula the authors and patrons of the corruptions be named: Illyricus, Philip, Pfeffinger, Osiander, Major, Calvin, Peter Martyr, and Philip's letter to the Palatine. At the very least they should be pointed out to the Church and to posterity, so that young people reading books may be able to beware of the errors that conflict with the Formula of Concord.

units.la: Non est necesse ad generalem conuentū hoc reiicere, quia libri sunt in omnium manibus, qui corruptelas continent, & certamina sunt in Ecclesia, nō tātum de corruptelis, sed etiam de personis. Multi reiiciunt Caluinianum, & tamen Philippum cum epistola ad Palatinum defendunt: sed causas nostras in scripto nostro modestè annotaui mus. Monemus etiam, vt quidam Paragraphi, & quædam verba omittantur, vt de vitā dis vocabulis Accidentis & substātiæ: quia secum pugnāt. Nobilissimum Pauli dictum, Lex est pædagogia in Christum, Philippicè in formula exponitur de disciplina externa: cùm Lutherus illud de spirituali vsu legis luculeter exponat, & rectissimè. Quod operibus nostris conseruetur Fides, defendi non potest.In loco de persona Christi, omit ti velim vocabula scholastica, subiectiuè, formaliter, habituaLiter. Quotusquisque enim pastorû intelligit obscura illa vocabula, & metuo ne nouas pariant contentiones, &res commodè exponi potest, sine istarum vocū adminiculo. Beza talibus tendiculis insidiatur simplicioribus, &insidiosè ad istas sordes nos pertrahere vel inuitare conatur. Censeo igitur omittenda esse ista vocabula. Hæc fere est summa nostrarum admonitionum, cum petitione, vt decretū de abrogato corpore Doctrinæ Misnico, ne sit norma doctrinæ, & reiectis spuriis illis libris, Acta synodica, & quæ eius farinæ sunt intelligo, publicetur, & toti Ecclesiæ promulgetur. Spero te breui commonefactiones nostras visurū. Domini Vvigandi & pastorum consensum expecto. Certò statuas nos magnificere formulam concordiæ, & læto animo agnoscere Dei beneficium, qui nostris certaminibus præclarum dicit testimonium. Ardenti pectore precamur Deum, vt suo spiritu hunc sanctum conatum constituendi concordiā in Ecclesia prouehat, confirmet, & ad optatum finem fœlici successu perducat. Atque huiusmodi preces pro Electore Saxonie & sancto hoc conatu publice fiunt in nostris Ecclesiis. Ostendemus Deo nos iuuante nos nec quæsiuisse aliud, nec etiam nunc aliud quærere, quàm vt incorrupta doctrina Lutheri sine omni fermento transmittatur ad posteritatem: omnium iniuriarum & exiliorum per Dei gratiam pié obliuiscemur. Iacobus Andreæ, Selneccerus, Crellius, si serió pœnit entiam agunt, fratres nobis erunt charissimi. Quòd si etiam Philippi, Pfeffinge ri, Maioris nomina sine detrimento Ecclesiæ silentio prætereri possent, simpliciter assentiremur. Nec nos voluptatem nec emolumentum speramus, si nominatim ponatur, Philippi sententiam de libero arbitrio & Cœna Domini aduersari verbo Dei. Quia verò videmus subesse grauissimas & necessarias causas, & exempla habemus Apostolorum Christi, veteris Ecclesiæ, humiliter petimus & rogamus, vt consulatur Iuuentuti nondum confirmato iudicio legenti libros Philippi, & vti posteritati. Et hactenus de communi causa Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: It is not necessary to reject these books by a general council, since the books containing the corruptions are in everyone's hands, and the disputes in the Church concern not only the corruptions but also persons. Many reject the Calvinian teaching, and yet defend Philip and his letter to the Palatine. We have noted our reasons modestly in our written statement. We also advise that certain paragraphs and certain words be omitted, such as those about the terms "accident" and "substance," because they contradict one another. Paul's noble saying, "The law is our schoolmaster to bring us to Christ," is expounded in the Formula in the Philippist manner, of external discipline, whereas Luther expounds it brilliantly and most rightly of the spiritual use of the law. That faith is preserved by our works cannot be defended. In the passage on the person of Christ I would like the scholastic words "subjectively," "formally," and "habitually" to be omitted. How few of the ministers understand those obscure words! I fear they will give rise to new contentions, whereas the matter can be explained well enough without the help of those terms. Beza lays snares with such nets for simpler people, and insidiously tries to draw us, or invite us, into those filths. I think, therefore, these words should be omitted. This is about the sum of our admonitions, together with the request that the decree on the abrogated Corpus of Doctrine of Meissen be made so that it is no longer a norm of doctrine; that those spurious books, the Synodal Acts and whatever is of that sort, be rejected, I understand; and that the decree be published and promulgated to the whole Church. I hope to see our admonitions shortly, and I await the agreement of Master Wigand and the ministers. Be assured that we magnify the Formula of Concord and gladly acknowledge God's benefit, who has given a noble testimony to our struggles. With burning hearts we pray God that by his Spirit he may advance and confirm this holy effort to establish concord in the Church, and bring it to the desired end with a happy outcome. Such prayers are indeed offered publicly in our churches for the Elector of Saxony and for this holy undertaking. We will show, with God's help, that we have neither sought nor now seek anything other than that the uncorrupted doctrine of Luther be handed down to posterity without any leaven. All injuries and exiles we will devoutly forget, by God's grace. Jacob Andreae, Selneccerus and Crellius, if they seriously repent, will be most dear brothers to us. But if the names of Philip, Pfeffinger and Major could be passed over in silence without harm to the Church, we would simply assent. We hope for neither pleasure nor advantage if it is named explicitly that Philip's opinion on free will and the Lord's Supper is contrary to the Word of God. But since we see that very grave and necessary causes lie behind this, and we have the examples of Christ's apostles and of the ancient Church, we humbly ask and beg that care be taken for the young, not yet of settled judgement, who read Philip's books, and for posterity. And so much concerning the common cause of the Church.

units.la: Nunc quedam de statu Ecclesiæ in Borus sia.magna tranquillitate frui possemus, si illi ferió pacem colerent, qui pacis se profitentur præcones, tres pastores, quorum duxest Morgenstein, Sax. & Schlusselburgius, gravem mihi litem mouent. & per totam Borufiam tumultum excitarunt, ob φρασιν in abstracto, scripto vehementi & inerudito & prolixo me adorti sunt, & atrociter deformarunt. Contendunt Abstractum separare naturas in Christo, diuidere personam, constituere duos omnipotentes. Nulla institutio, nulla admonitio locum apud illos inuenit. Lutheri & Morlini authoritatem mihi obiiciunt, respondi illis, varie vsurpari vocabulum Abstracti. Lutherum aliquoties iuxta Etymon pro separatione vsurpasse. Alias vero scholastice vsurpari pro distinctione vocum, Deus & Diuinitas, Homo & Humanitas. In Abstracto est locutio, quando de humanitate Christi in ipsa vnione fit mentio. Monstraui exempla aliorum, qui vocabulo isto scholastice sunt usi, nihil tamen profeci. Aliud enim subest quantum video. Dominus wigandus dudum eos reprimere potuisset, sed siluit & conniuendo eos confirmauit. V Vigandus hanc propositionem concedit, non tantum in concreto recte dicitur, Homo Christus est omnipotens, Viuificus, ado-ran-
units.tr: Now a few things about the state of the Church in Prussia. We could enjoy great tranquillity if those who profess themselves heralds of peace would seriously cultivate peace. Three ministers, of whom the leader is Morgenstein, a Saxon, and Schlüsselburg, stir up a grave quarrel against me and have roused tumult throughout all Prussia. On account of the expression "in the abstract" they attacked me in a vehement, unlearned and lengthy writing, and savagely misrepresented me. They contend that "the abstract" separates the natures in Christ, divides the person, and makes two omnipotent beings. No instruction and no admonition finds a place with them. They object to me the authority of Luther and of Morlin. I answered them that the word "abstract" is used in various ways: that Luther sometimes used it according to its etymology, for separation; but otherwise it is used in the scholastic sense for the distinction of terms, God and Deity, Man and Humanity. "In the abstract" is an expression used when the humanity of Christ is mentioned in the union itself. I showed examples of others who had used the word in the scholastic sense, yet I accomplished nothing. For something else lies beneath, as far as I can see. Master Wigand could have restrained them long ago, but he kept silent and, by conniving, confirmed them. Wigand concedes this proposition: not only in the concrete is it rightly said, "Christ, the man, is omnipotent, life-giving, adorable,"

units.la: {y} randus. Sed etiam in abstracto dicitur recte, Humanitas Christi est omnipotens, Viuifica & adoranda. Et hoc tantum dixi, cothurnum VVitebergensium detegere volens. Pastores hoc impugnarunt, vt ipsorum scriptu docet, & tamen non repressit eos: fingunt nunc nouum controuersiae statum, quasi dixerim, Humanitatem Christi in abstracto esse adorandam, & abstractum ad praedicatum de adoratione attulerim, quod mihi in mentem non venit. Tantum enim subiecti est declaratio. Abstractum inquiunt scholastici, supponit pro natura. Consiliarij cupiunt controuersiam componere. D. Ionas & D. Cancellarius & alij docti fatentur mihi iniuriam fieri. Reliqui fatentur se non intelligere, vix agnoscent pastores se ignscitia lapsos esse. Quid futurum sit dies docebit. Aliquoties testatus sum in publica lectione & scripto, me de vocabulo non pugnare. Verum nec hoc satis est eis. Affectibus ergo indulgent, quia me traduxerunt, quasi diuidere personam: aliquanto acrius eis respondi latine, vt eorum audaciam reprimerem. Sed quantum intelligo, non remittunt vehementiam: gloriantur se habere manum Chemnicij, qua testeris te improbare meam sententiam & vocis vsum. Ego adduci nō possum vt credam. In tuis enim literis ad me testa- tus es, vos idem sentire, & epistola Stamichij quid aliud vult? Scholastico sensu vocabuli Abstracti sine separatione naturarum aliquoties es visus in libello de duabus naturis in Christo. Ego de voce non pugno, per me licet sepeliatur, sed hoc ferendum mihi nullo modo est, quod isti homines ex insciitia vocis me traduxerunt, quasi diuiderem personam Christi & duos constituere Christos, hic nemo iubet me patientem esse. Extremae enim blasphemiae est diuidere personam Christi, & segregare naturas. Verum sic excipitur fidelis Episcopusin Boruffia, & qui dem apaitoribus. Hanc reporto gratia quod confessionem oppolui Sophismatis & conuitiis Caluinistarum.
units.tr: but also in the abstract it is rightly said, "The humanity of Christ is omnipotent, life-giving and adorable." I said only this, wishing to expose the buskin of the Wittenbergers. The ministers opposed this, as their writing shows, and yet he did not restrain them. Now they invent a new state of the controversy, as if I had said that the humanity of Christ is to be adored in the abstract, and had brought "abstract" to the predicate of adoration, which never came into my mind. For there is only a declaration of the subject. They say that the scholastics hold that "the abstract" stands for the nature. Counsellors desire to settle the controversy. Dr Jonas, the Chancellor and other learned men admit that an injustice is being done to me. The rest admit they do not understand, and the ministers will hardly acknowledge that they have fallen through ignorance. What will happen the day will show. Several times I have testified, in public lecture and in writing, that I do not quarrel about a word. But even this is not enough for them. So they indulge their passions, because they have misrepresented me as if I divided the person. I answered them somewhat more sharply in Latin, to restrain their audacity. But as far as I understand, they do not relent in their vehemence; they boast that they have Chemnitz's hand, by which you bear witness that you disapprove of my opinion and of my use of the word. I cannot bring myself to believe it. For in your letters to me you testified that we think the same, and what does Stamichius's letter mean? In the scholastic sense of the word "abstract," without separation of the natures, you have several times appeared to agree in your little book on the two natures in Christ. I do not quarrel about the word; let it be buried, for all I care. But this I can by no means bear: that these men, through ignorance of the term, have misrepresented me as if I divided the person of Christ and made two Christs. Here no one bids me be patient. For it is the extreme of blasphemy to divide the person of Christ and to sever the natures. But thus is the faithful bishop received in Prussia, and indeed by ministers. I gain this much from it, that I opposed the confession to the sophisms and insults of the Calvinists.

units.la: Kirchnerus licet controuersiam non intelligat, vt noui hominem, tamen superbas ad me scripsit literas, leges dictans potificiali ter, & meos Antagonistas insicitia stabilien- do, non parum turbauit hanc Ecclesiam: Monere eum potes, vt deinceps cautius & magis fraterne agat. Tarditatem responsionis epistolę compenso, quanquam hęc poste riora minus grata tibi futura sunt: sed talis est fortuna Doctorum, vbi ex acie reuertun- tur, vbi cum hostibus pugnarunt, à domes- ficis sticis & fratribus aliquanto durius tractan-tur, quàm ab hostibus.
units.tr: Kirchner, although he does not understand the controversy (as I know the man), has nevertheless written me haughty letters, dictating laws pontifically and asserting that my opponents are ignorant. He has not a little disturbed this Church. You may advise him to act more cautiously and more brotherly from now on. I make up for the delay in my reply, although these later matters will be less welcome to you. But such is the lot of teachers: when they return from the battle line, where they have fought with the enemy, they are treated somewhat more harshly by their own household and brothers than by the enemy.

units.la: Christus ergo confirmet animum, & re-primat tetras calumnias: Ego distinguo inter scholasticum vsum vocabuli Abstracti, quando alterutra natura cósideratur vel no minatur, vt Diuinitas vel humanitas, & Etymologicum de separatione, vt Lutherus & Morlinus pio sensu vsurparunt. V Vigan dus abstractum aliàs ad subiectum refert, ac tum probat, aliàs ad prædicatum, & tum improbat, quantum de separatione intelligitur. Hæc quantum videre possum eodem recidunt. An nō igitur ob inanem λογομαχίαν turbent Ecclesiam, Dominus iudicet: sententiam tuam de hac distinctione expeto. Non video quomodo aliàs loca in tuo libello, §. loca in Luthero (hic tacendum est de abstracto) conciliari possint.
units.tr: May Christ then strengthen my spirit and repress these foul calumnies. I distinguish between the scholastic use of the term "abstract", when either nature is considered or named, such as divinity or humanity, and the etymological sense of separation, which Luther and Morlin used in a pious sense. Vigandus sometimes refers the abstract to the subject and then approves it, and sometimes to the predicate and then disapproves it, insofar as it is understood as separation. As far as I can see, these come to the same thing. Whether they disturb the Church over an empty word-battle [λογομαχίαν], let the Lord judge. I desire your opinion on this distinction. I do not see how the passages in your little book, the section on the passages in Luther (here one must be silent about the abstract), can otherwise be reconciled.

units.la: Quia Imperator Ratisbonæ moram nectit, defatigati ordines Regni Poloniæ in Stephanum Batorium regem consenserunt, & is nunc rerum potitur. Nuper Regia eius Maiestas transiit Marienwerdt, vbi principis nostri legati eius Maiestatem conuenerunt, & quantum intelligo pro rege agnoue runt, & de commeatu prouiderunt. Gedanenses obstina tè se opponunt Regi Batorio quibus rebus freti, ignoro. Daniæ Regē metuunt credo, cuius beneuolentia difficulter carere possunt. Difficile erit Imperatori Regem Poloniæ potentem pellere, & Turcam prouocare. Nobis vero imminet Moscus. Nos precamur Filium Dei, vt pacem Ecclesiæ largiatur. Tu nos iuua precibus. Benè in Domino Vale. Regiomonte Borussiorum 10. Septembris 1576.
units.tr: Because the Emperor is delaying at Regensburg, the wearied estates of the Kingdom of Poland have agreed to Stephen Batory as king, and he now holds power. Recently His Royal Majesty passed through Marienwerder, where the legates of our prince met his Majesty and, as far as I understand, acknowledged him as king and made provision for supplies. The Danzigers stubbornly oppose King Batory, and on what grounds I do not know. I suppose they fear the King of Denmark, whose goodwill they can hardly do without. It will be difficult for the Emperor to drive out a powerful King of Poland and to provoke the Turk. Muscovy, however, threatens us. We pray the Son of God to grant peace to the Church. Help us with your prayers. Farewell in the Lord. At Königsberg in Prussia, 10 September 1576.

units.la: Tilemanus Heshusius Episcopus Sambiensis.
units.tr: Tilemann Heshusius, Bishop of Samland.

units.la: DISP V.
units.tr: DISP V.

units.la: DISPVTATIO DE MAIESTATE HOMINIS CHRISti, ad normam verae piaeque doctrinae per Theses explicata, aduersus impias Iacobi Andreae Schmidelini Theses, Tubingae olim propositas.
units.tr: A DISPUTATION CONCERNING THE MAJESTY OF THE HUMAN NATURE OF CHRIST, explained by theses according to the rule of true and pious doctrine, against the impious theses of Jakob Andreas Schmidelin, formerly put forward at Tübingen.

units.la: Ingolstadij primùm anno M.D.LXIIII excusa. Deinde anno LXXI. witebergae iussu rectoris fecundò, ac nunc hìc tertiò, propter graues causas, recusa.
units.tr: First printed at Ingolstadt in the year 1564. Then reprinted a second time in the year 1571 at Wittenberg by order of the rector, and now here for a third time, reprinted on account of serious reasons.

units.la: Æquus iudicet Lector, & veritatem contra falsitatem ingenuè tueatur.
units.tr: Let the fair-minded reader judge, and honestly defend truth against falsehood.

units.la: PRÆFATIO AVTHORIS.
units.tr: PREFACE OF THE AUTHOR.

units.la: Ircumferuntur dogmata quædam, authore Schmidelino, de Maiestate hominis Christi, non quæ Apostoli docuerunt, sed nouaplane & perniciosa, & cum Christi, Apostolorum, Prophetarum, Martyrum, Confessorum, & cum omnium denique totius ecclesiæ Catholicæ Patrum doctrina ex diametro pugnantia. Quoniam vero Apostolus grauiter monet, ne doctrinis variis & peregrinis abducamur, iubétq. doctrinam, quæ secundum pietatem est, tueri saluam in ecclesia: operam nos, neque inutilem, neque à professione nostra alienam, sumpturos existimauimus, si aduersus nouos & impios Schmidelini errores, veram & Orthodoxam Ecclesiæ sententiam vin dicaremus. Proponimus ergo Theses, vt ille fecit, sed meliore fide tractaturi graue hoc & scitu dignum Argumentum. Ac duplicem quidem ordinem thesium posuimus, vt primum haberet lectorem totius negotij, quod plerisque forsan obscurum videbitur, necessariam explicationem: deinde vero, vt de Schmidelini ineptiis, imò aperta & horrenda impietate, boni omnes rectius iudicarent. Quare theses alias explicatorias, alias confutatorias fecimus.
units.tr: There are circulating certain doctrines, put forward by Schmidelin, concerning the majesty of the man Christ. They are not what the Apostles taught; they are entirely new and pernicious, and they flatly contradict the teaching of Christ, the Apostles, the Prophets, the Martyrs and Confessors, and, in short, of all the Fathers of the whole Catholic Church. Since the Apostle warns us gravely not to be carried away by various and strange teachings, and bids us keep the doctrine which accords with godliness safe in the Church, we have judged that we would undertake a work that is neither useless nor foreign to our profession, if we defended the true and Orthodox opinion of the Church against the new and impious errors of Schmidelin. We therefore propose Theses, as he did, but we shall treat this serious and worthy subject in better good faith. We have set out the theses in two orders: first, so that the reader who will perhaps find the whole matter obscure may have a necessary explanation; and then, so that all good people may judge more rightly of Schmidelin's absurdities, or rather his open and horrible impiety. Accordingly, we have made some theses explanatory and others confutatory.

units.la: Hunc nostrum laborem quisquis es veritatis studiosus boni vt consulas per Christum rogamus. Ingolstadij Calendis Iulij, Salutis Anno M. D. LXIIII.
units.tr: We ask you, whoever you are that love the truth, to take this our labour in good part, through Christ. Ingolstadt, on the Kalends of July, in the year of salvation 1564.

units.la: EX
units.tr: FROM

units.la: THESES EXPLICATORIÆ DE MAIESTATE HOminis Christi.
units.tr: Explanatory Theses on the Majesty of the Man Christ.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: CUM omnis hæc de Maiestate Christi hominis Christi disputatio ex hypostatica duarum naturarum in Christo vnione peti debeat & intelligi, res ipsa postulare videtur, vt ante omnia discrimen, quod inter hypostasin & naturam intercedit, hoc loco repetamus & animaduertamus. Quod sane discrimen si negligatur, non minus erit nobis periculi, quàm plerisque accidit in illo veterum Hæresiarcharum albo, qui inter hypostasin & οὐσίαν non distinguentes, in varios, eósque pudendos & impios errores impegerunt.
units.tr: Since the whole of this discussion of the majesty of the man Christ must be sought and understood from the hypostatic union of the two natures in Christ, the matter itself seems to require that, before everything else, we recall and note here the distinction between hypostasis and nature. If this distinction is neglected, we shall run no less risk than many did in that roll of the old heresiarchs who, failing to distinguish between hypostasis and οὐσία [ousia], fell into various, shameful and impious errors.

units.la: 2 Sic Arriani dum ex personarum Trinitate, naturarum Trinitatem inferunt: Filium à Patre, & Spiritum sanctum ab vtroq. ἑτεροούσιον astruunt. E diuerso Sabelliani quoniam ex vna τειάδος
units.tr: 2 Thus the Arians, while inferring a Trinity of natures from a Trinity of persons, maintain that the Son and the Holy Spirit are of a different essence [ἑτεροούσιον] from the Father. On the other side, the Sabellians, because from one Triad [τριάδος] they keep gathering one hypostasis,

units.la: E οὐσίᾳ vnam subinde hypostasin colligūt, non solum Filium, sed & Patrem & Spiritum sanctum incarnatos ac passos esse confingūt. Sic & Nestoriani, dum ex duabus Christi naturis duas in Christo hypostases faciunt, non καθ' ὑπόστασιν, sed κατὰ συμβεβηκὸς Deum cum homine coniungunt. Contrà verò, Eutychiani, dum ex vna Christi hypostasi vnam quoq. naturam deducunt, vnā tantum οὐσίαν, quemadmodum & vnam personam in Christo Domino constituunt atque definiunt.
units.tr: from one essence [οὐσίᾳ] they keep gathering one hypostasis, and so pretend that not only the Son but also the Father and the Holy Spirit were incarnate and suffered. So too the Nestorians, while making two hypostases in Christ out of his two natures, join God with man not according to hypostasis but according to accident [κατὰ συμβεβηκὸς]. On the contrary, the Eutychians, while deducing one nature from the one hypostasis of Christ, also set up and define one essence and one person in the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: 3 Nec sanè dissimilis fuit Monothelitarum inscitia, qui dum vnam duntaxat in Christo personam contra Nestorium: duas verò naturas, contra Eutychetem re ste profitentur: rati tamen, ad personæ vnitatem, proprietatis quoque & operationis vnitatem esse necessariam, quò Nestorij herefin declinent, vnam tantum vtriusque naturæ proprietatem atque operationem, ob personæ vnitate in Christo constituunt, atque ita vtriusque naturæ proprietates non minus imperitè quā impiè confundunt.
units.tr: 3 The ignorance of the Monothelites was no less similar. While they profess, against Nestorius, only one person in Christ, and, against Eutyches, two natures, they nonetheless think that, for the unity of the person, a unity of property and of operation is also necessary, so that they may avoid the heresy of Nestorius. Therefore they posit, because of the unity of the person in Christ, only one property and one operation of both natures, and so confuse the properties of both natures, as unskilfully as they do impiously.

units.la: 4 Quamuis verò natura, substantia, essentia seu οὐσία (quæ promiscuè in hac tractatione, veterū more, passim vsurpabimus bimus) varias sortiantur significationes, si quis exacte nomina peruestiget, hic tame pro eo sumuntur, quod definitione, qua, quid res est, explicatur, comprehenditur.
units.tr: 4 Although nature, substance, essence or οὐσία [ousia] (which, in this treatment, after the manner of the ancients, we shall use interchangeably throughout) bear various meanings, if anyone examines the words exactly, here they are taken in the sense that is comprehended by the definition by which what a thing is, is explained.

units.la: 5 Natura itaque seu οὐσία ab hypostasi, quam Latini Theologi personae vel subsistentiae nomine solent appellare, eo distinguitur, quòd natura solam rei quid ditatem complectitur, quae ex se quidem multis indiuiduis est communis, totámq. οὐσιωδη singulorum perfectionem continet, cuiusmodi est, humanitas. Hypostasis vero dicitur indiuiduum, quod à cæteris omnib. eiusdem naturae singularib. quadã proprietate discretu, ita per se & in se exi stit, vt nulla ratione in altero sustentetur, aut sustetari queat, vt Petrus, Ioānes, &c.
units.tr: 5 Nature, or essence [οὐσία], is therefore distinguished from hypostasis, which the Latin theologians are accustomed to call by the name person or subsistence, in this way: nature embraces only the quiddity of a thing, which in itself is common to many individuals, and contains the essential [οὐσιωδη] perfection of each of them, as humanity does. Hypostasis, on the other hand, is called an individual which, distinguished from all the other singulars of the same nature by a certain property, exists through itself and in itself, so that it is in no way sustained in another, nor can be, as Peter, John, and so on.

units.la: 6 Vbi ne vocum ὁμωνυμία generet obscuritatem, accuratè discernendum est inter eas proprietates, quas προσωπικὰς, & eas, quas οὐσιώδεις vocant. Nam in explicatione personae, non de essentialibus, sed de personalibus locuti sumus.
units.tr: 6 Here, lest homonymy [ὁμωνυμία] produce obscurity, we must carefully distinguish between those properties which are called personal [προσωπικὰς] and those which are called essential [οὐσιώδεις]. For in explaining the person, we spoke not of the essential but of the personal.

units.la: 7 Ex hac porrò distinctione id com primis manifestum euadit, quanam ratione, vnam quidem οὐσίαν contra Arium, & tres hypostases contra Sabelliũ, in sacrosancta Triade profiteamur: eò nimirum, quòd vna tantùm eadémque sim-pliciffima in augustissimo illo Trinitatis mysterio communis effentia reperiatur, quæ totam in fe deitatis continet perse-ctionem: tres verò proprietates personales, quibus tres personæ constituuntur ac inter sese distinguuntur.
units.tr: 7 From this distinction it becomes clear above all why, in the most holy Trinity, we profess one οὐσία [ousia] against Arius, and three hypostases against Sabellius: namely, because in that most august mystery of the Trinity only one, and that most simple, common essence is found, which contains in itself the whole perfection of the deity, whereas the three personal properties are those by which the three persons are constituted and distinguished from one another.

units.la: 8 Veruntamen sanctissimæ Trinitatis sacramentum plane est incomparabile, adeóque rerum naturam, omnémque mentis humanæ, imò & angelicæ capacitatem in immensum excedit, in eo, quòd effentia illa in tribus diuinis personis sub sistens, non specie aut sola ratione, vna, sicut in creaturis vfuuenit, sed vna fit penitus atque fimpliciffima.
units.tr: 8 Nevertheless, the sacrament of the most holy Trinity is altogether incomparable, and so far exceeds the nature of things and the capacity of every human mind, and even of the angelic mind, in that this essence, subsisting in the three divine persons, is not one in species or merely in concept, as it is found in creatures, but is wholly and most simply one.

units.la: 9 Hinc & illud fit perspicuum, aliud esse, quædam in vnam eandémque naturam vniri, aliud verò in personæ vnitatem coagmentari. Illa siquidem in natura dicimus vnita, quæ in vna conueniunt οὐσία, fiue id fiat absque vlla concretione, miftione aut conuersione, vt in diuinis personis inuenitur: fiue sola compositione, vt in hominis ex anima & corpore constitutione: fiue denique intercedente mixtione aliqua, confusione aut conuersione, vt in elementorum tranfmutatione & ne & mixtorum productione accidere constat.
units.tr: 9 From this also it becomes plain that it is one thing for certain things to be united in one and the same nature, and another for them to be joined together into a unity of person. For we say that those things are united in nature which come together in one οὐσία [ousia], whether this happens without any concretion, mixture or conversion, as is found in the divine persons; or by mere composition, as in the constitution of a man from soul and body; or finally with some intervening mixture, confusion or conversion, as is clearly the case in the transmutation of the elements and the production of mixed bodies.

units.la: 10 At vero illa in hypostasi vnita es se dicimus, quæ ad eum modum sunt coniuncta, vt eadem prorsus existant subsistentia: Cuius generis est animi atque corporis in vno aliquo homine compositio. Præterquam enim quòd hæc tanquam partes essentiales ad naturæ vnius perfectionem coeunt, in vna quoque persona connectuntur, cum vna vtrique communis sit subsistentia.
units.tr: 10 But we say that those things are united in hypostasis which are so joined that they exist as one and the same subsistence. Of this kind is the composition of soul and body in some one man. For apart from the fact that these, as essential parts, come together to make up the perfection of one nature, they are also connected in one person, since one subsistence is common to both.

units.la: 11 Iam vero vt ad rem ipsam aliquanto propius accedamus, veramque & Catholicam de duarum naturarum in Christo vnione sententiam explicemus. Credimus in primis, vnanimiq; consensu profitemur Christiani, duas naturas, diuinam, inquam, & humanam in vno Christo hypostaticos vnitas esse: eam autem vnionem ideo cum sancta & Apostolica Ecclesia hypostaticam seu personalem appellamus, quòd duæ illæ naturæ secundum subsistentiam in Christo vnitæ sint, vt sacrosanctæ generales Synodi iampridem definiere. Sic enim in Ephesina Synodo decretum est: Carni secundum subsistentiam vnitum est Dei Patris verbum. Et in
units.tr: 11 Now, so that we may approach the matter itself somewhat more closely and explain the true and Catholic view of the union of the two natures in Christ: we Christians believe first of all, and profess with one accord, that the two natures, the divine, I mean, and the human, are united hypostatically in the one Christ. We call that union hypostatic or personal with the holy and Apostolic Church, because those two natures are united in Christ according to subsistence, as the holy general synods long ago defined. For thus it was decreed in the Synod of Ephesus: the Word of God is united to flesh according to subsistence. And in

units.la: E.iij. quinta Synodo generali: Sancta vero Dei Ecclesia, utriusque scilicet Nestorij & Eutychetis perfidiæ impietatem eiiciens, unitionem Dei verbi ad carnem secundum compositionem confitetur, quod est secundum subsistentiam. Et sequenti Canone: Si quis non confitetur Dei verbum carni subsistentialiter uniri, & propterea unam eius subsistentiam vel unam personam, & ita sanctam Chalcedonensem Synodum unam subsistentiam Domini nostri IESV Christi confiteri, talis anathema sit. In Decretis etiam Synodalibus Martini primi sic habetur: Si quis non confitetur secundum sanctos Patres proprie & vere ex duabus naturis Deitate & humanitate secundum subsistentiam unitis, inconfuse & indiuise eundem & unum Dominum nostrum IESVM Christum esse, sit condemnatus.
